transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-11-02
Time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen, Marco Ruiz, Priya Nair, Ethan Park, Jamal Brooks, Selina Gomez, Rita Li
Shared artifacts: se-messaging-v2 deck (https://redwood.ai/sales/decks/se-messaging-v2), competitive-battlecards.xlsx (drive link), demo-recording-template.mp4

[00:00] Avery: ok hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll run through the updated messaging, call out the competitor points and then run two short demo plays. Try to keep feedback tight so we can capture changes.
[00:18] Priya: yep hi all, i'll open the deck — slide 3 has the new 30-second positioning blurb, put it in the notes: "Redwood is the developer-first inference platform that makes inference predictable and economical across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments".
[00:32] Jamal: quick q — that sentence is great, but customers always ask, like, what's the difference vs Anthropic or Vertex? can we put a faster follow-up?
[00:40] Priya: good point — slide 4 has the short answer: "We focus on serving: predictable latency, lower unit cost via batching/caching, and unified controls across deployment types". Add the timeframe: "prod-ready in days, not months" for demo language.
[01:05] Marco: uh and i'll flag the technical tie-ins when we demo — highlight KV cache, continuous batching, kernel selection. but careful, when we say KV cache some folks hear "KV cash" in demos, so pronounce clearly.
[01:22] Selina: hah yeah i've had that. Also in competitive calls we need the quick rebuttal to pricing objections: e.g., "we beat API-only costs at scale because of intelligent batching and quantization recommendations".
[01:40] Priya: i'll add that to bullets. we should also add a line about routing/fallbacks — customers love reliability stories: canary A/B, automated fallback to cheaper model variant.
[01:58] Avery: perfect. ok demo 1 — Marco you take the hosted->dedicated failover scenario? recreate a threshold where capacity hits the limit and we route to a cheaper variant.
[02:12] Marco: yep. starting the demo — shared screen now.
[02:20] [02:20] Marco (screen): starting load test ... injecting latency ... showing route policy in Console -> Policies -> Smart routing. note: console UI is a little out of date in the deck.
[03:15] Marco: we hit spike, automatic fallback to gpt-like-open-variant, routing rules show reason code, request continues — latency goes up slightly, cost drops 40%.
[03:34] Jamal: nice. what's the customer-visible SLO here?
[03:40] Marco: we keep P95 under 300ms for cached prefixes; worst-case cold start might hit 800ms — depends on model and sequence length. say that in words: "we trade a small latency bump for availability and cost savings".
[03:58] Priya: capture that phrasing. Also add the audit trail note — every routing decision is logged in request traces and console — useful for security/compliance questions.
[04:20] Selina: shout re: SOC2 — we need to remind folks to always bring up the SOC2 + KMS integration in the second slide for enterprise. sometimes SEs skip it.
[04:34] Avery: yes put that as an ask in playbook. okay quick role-play — Jamal you be the procurement lead and i’ll be the AE.
[04:45] Jamal: ok um so, procurement: "what about data residency? we need EU-only hosting and audit logs".
[04:54] Avery: short answer: "we offer region pinning for hosted, and Private gives you VPC + customer-managed KMS and audit logs". we also have an on-prem package for air-gapped needs.
[05:12] Jamal: customer will then ask about encryption at rest and HSM.
[05:18] Avery: reply: "we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key control and store minimal logs — also support per-tenant encryption keys".
[05:27] Marco: note: in technical deep dives we should be ready to explain key rotation and access patterns. keep it simple on calls.
[05:36] Priya: moving on, demo 2 — private deployment walk-through (V P C flow + deployment). Marco?
[05:45] Marco: yep. sharing screen. starting with onboarding playbook — show network diagram: control plane (managed) vs dataplane (customer VPC). sometimes the slide says "control lane" which is wrong, so update.
[06:10] Marco: show the quickstart: customer provisions subnets, we give helm chart, there's a connector that establishes mTLS tunnel to control plane.
[06:28] Rita: are there any firewall changes needed?
[06:31] Marco: typically open egress to our control plane endpoints on 443, and open mutual TLS port for the agent. we document the ports in the security whitepaper. link in chat.
[06:42] Selina: and SSO? enterprise always asks SAML/SCIM.
[06:46] Avery: yes SAML + SCIM supported for RBAC — include that in slide 6.
[06:51] [07:00] Side note: transcription glitch: "KV cache" transcribed as "KV cash" in the live caption — we'll mark that to fix in post.
[07:10] Priya: ok show of hands — biggest competitor messaging hole? Jamal?
[07:14] Jamal: customers bring up OpenAI a lot. their play is simplicity + model quality. our answer: "if model quality is primary and you need rapid experimentation, we support that, but when you care about production economics and predictable SLAs, Redwood wins".
[07:35] Selina: add a concise soundbite: "Own the serving, not the model" — or maybe that's a bit marketing-y.
[07:45] Priya: i like "Serving, not just models" — shorter.
[07:52] Marco: quick tech point for SEs: when asked about latency vs cost, use this pattern: 1) ask for P95 target and token distribution, 2) explain batching/caching levers, 3) propose Dedicated or Private for strict SLOs.
[08:10] Avery: role-play 2 — i’ll be the skeptical engineer. Jamal you demo.
[08:18] Jamal: ok, so "why can't i just host a model on VM X and build inference?"
[08:23] Jamal (as customer): "we tried that, inconsistent latencies and high ops overhead".
[08:28] Jamal: response: "most customers underestimate the operational cost: autoscaling edgecases, kernel tuning, and caching strategies. Redwood's runtime gives continuous batching, quantization profiles, and kernel selection out of the box".
[08:40] Rita: someone asked earlier about benchmarks — do we have a public benchmark?
[08:44] Marco: we have internal perf sheets, and a curated catalog with verified profiles. we should avoid calling it "public benchmark" unless it's on the site. say "verified performance profiles" instead.
[08:55] Priya: good. also, add a slide with a simple cost example: 100M tokens/month — hosted vs dedicated cost delta. Ethan can pull numbers and add to the playbook.
[09:05] Ethan: on it — i'll add a table and a short paragraph explaining assumptions (seq length, tokenization).
[09:12] [09:30] Interruption — team chat: Marco: "i'll mute for a sec, hold on" — brief audio glitch.
[09:50] Marco: back. ok final section: competitive objections and canned rebuttals. Priya read them out.
[10:00] Priya: Objection: "We need absolute on-prem control"; Rebuttal: "Private deployment with on-prem option; we offer air-gapped package and full audit logs".
[10:20] Priya: Objection: "Your unit cost is higher than raw EC2"; Rebuttal: "At scale raw EC2 costs more when you factor ops; we provide batching/caching/quantization guidance that reduces per-token cost".
[10:35] Selina: add a one-liner about regression monitoring and eval hooks — clients want quality guardrails.
[10:42] Marco: yep: "built-in evals and prompt test suites that tie to regressions and rollbacks".
[10:50] Avery: demo practice takeaway — record two short clips: routing/fallback & private-onboarding. Marco you'll do them.
[11:00] Priya: marketing ask: can we make the quick rebuttal lines accessible in Slack snippet format? Like 2-3 lines with bullets.
[11:08] Avery: yes, Priya will post them.
[11:15] Jamal: i have one thing — during live demos, avoid showing raw error logs that reference internal service names. scrub before presenting.
[11:25] Marco: noted. use demo account + anonymized logs.
[11:30] Avery: ok let's recap.
[11:32] Avery: recap: Priya updates deck + posts Slack snippet (due 11/04), Marco records two demo clips (due 11/08), Ethan publishes cost-table in playbook (due 11/05), Avery schedules role-play sessions. We'll also update slide copy for SOC2/KMS/SAML.
[11:52] Selina: thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[11:55] Rita: thanks — quick follow-up, can someone share the links?
[11:58] Priya: i'll drop the links in the thread after this meeting.
[12:00] Avery: thanks team, meeting adjourned.

Notes about transcript: natural disfluency retained; occasional small transcription errors (KV cash, V P C spaced) to reflect real captions. Action items captured above.
